source.scope: All 20 printed MPh ASOP steps and identified supplemental in-volume rule families. Scenario SSRs, individual equipment notes and external modules require profile-specific reconciliation.

groups: 3.22A · Select a ground mover and declarations

options.title: Commit one expenditure, then resolve responses
options.prompt: What is being spent now, and whose decision follows?
checks: Keep the route proposal separate from committed expenditures. Entering a hex and Recovering a weapon are separate actions, even in the same Location.
Record the actual MF/MP cost, route, facing and participating units. Complete an impulse’s expenditures before First Fire.
Resolve triggered effects and the defender’s current response before the next expenditure. A pass closes only this window, not later windows or the entire MPh.
options.effect: A live component needs distinct Continue movement, End this unit’s move and End phase actions, with Rules-owned gates. This reference preview only records consideration.
options.example: A squad enters for 1 MF, then wants to Recover a SW for another MF. The defender gets the entry response before Recovery is committed.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.
options.timing: Rule-specific MPh timing; supplemental to ASOP

options.title: Choose the next mover without skipping compulsory movement
options.prompt: Which movement sequence must finish before another begins?
checks: Complete all units that began THE MPh berserk before any non-berserk unit starts ITS MPh.
Complete ground movement before aerial glider/parachute sequences. Revisit currently berserk units at 3.21A; newly created berserk states can interrupt other procedures.
Within a printed step, choose the order unless a rule says otherwise. Do not combine different units into a stack merely to share a completed checklist.
options.effect: Track a separate movement instance for each unit/stack and the appropriate group procedure. No moving units is a valid transition only after required work is settled.
options.example: An unmoved berserk squad prevents starting an ordinary tank’s move. A later berserk result requires its own source-governed interruption.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.
options.timing: Rule-specific MPh timing; supplemental to ASOP

options.title: Replace a lost or non-Good-Order mortar Spotter
options.prompt: Does a mortar need a replacement Spotter?
checks: This opening window replaces a Spotter eliminated or no longer in Good Order.
Check spotting qualifications and commitments under C9.3; do not treat this as unrestricted mid-move designation.
options.effect: Associate the replacement with its mortar and preserve all spotting commitments.
options.example: A broken Spotter can trigger this opening review before any unit starts moving.

options.title: Attempt opening defender Starshells
options.prompt: Would illumination matter before the attacker starts moving?
checks: Evaluate eligible leaders, MMC and CE AFV in this opening window.
Keep placement, usage and illumination results separate from later restricted attempts.
options.effect: Recompute disclosed illumination and LOS before the first move.
options.example: The defender considers an eligible Starshell before the attacker selects its first mover.

options.title: Place aerial gliders at their intended landing hexes
options.prompt: Are incoming gliders represented in their aerial Locations?
checks: Place all applicable gliders blue side up at their ILH.
Placement does not bypass ground movement or begin landing; the aerial response sequence comes later.
options.effect: Keep gliders queued for 3.23A and 3.37D after ground movement.
options.example: A glider appears at its ILH now, but the ground units finish their MPh first.

options.title: Prepare the next required berserk charge
options.prompt: Is there a currently berserk unit required to charge?
checks: Determine the legal charge target and route using the berserk rules and Known enemy information.
Enter 3.31A for that charge; only proceed to ordinary selection if no such unit can charge.
options.effect: Do not offer a general decline as an alternative to a compulsory charge.
options.example: After a fire result creates a berserk unit, the guide revisits charge obligations rather than keeping a stale ordinary move plan.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Select an eligible unit, stack or group
options.prompt: Who can move, and what commitments already limit them?
checks: Check Good Order/Mobile status, pinned Infantry and Prep/Bounding Fire or TI commitments; preserve explicit special-rule exceptions.
Calculate MF/MP, portage, leader accompaniment and movement type. Do not restore already-spent MF merely because a SW is dropped.
Review road bonus, terrain and prior unloading restrictions from their own rules.
options.effect: Show available movement and the reason for known restrictions. Unknown terrain evaluation stays visible as not evaluated.
options.example: A squad that held fire may move; its neighboring Prep-firing squad cannot be treated as another ordinary mover.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Drop possession before moving
options.prompt: Should carried equipment be left before movement begins?
checks: Name the weapon and its Location; dropping possession is not a Rally transfer to another unit.
Recalculate starting portage correctly and retain any independent Recovery requirements for the next owner.
options.effect: Record ownership and load separately from movement allowance.
options.example: A squad leaves an MMG before starting; another unit still needs its own legal Recovery opportunity.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Check night Freedom of Movement
options.prompt: Is a night Scenario Defender unit free to move?
checks: Check the actual release conditions, including permitted attacks, Known enemy sightings and applicable sharing rules.
Offer the best eligible leader’s once-per-friendly-MPh dr only when E1.21 permits it; this is not a generic NTC.
Preserve acquired Freedom of Movement and distinguish Scenario Defender from this turn’s DEFENDER.
options.effect: Explain publicly known restrictions without revealing unseen opposing units.
options.example: A side now taking its Player Turn can still be the Scenario Defender and subject to night movement limits.

options.title: Resolve required Movement and Straying checks
options.prompt: Does night, jungle, bamboo or beach movement require a check?
checks: Use the applicable rule and unit conditions, rather than applying one universal night roll.
Resolve movement direction, restrictions and any Jitter trigger before continuing the intended route.
options.effect: Keep the intended route and the actual permitted route distinct.
options.example: A unit that planned to move north must follow a source-required Straying result instead.

options.title: Declare Double Time at the start
options.prompt: Is gaining two MF worth the CX consequences?
checks: Check eligibility and declare before the unit begins its movement.
Add the permitted two MF and CX; retain portage and other restrictions. Compare with the smaller later declaration.
options.effect: Show effects on later fire and CC as well as movement.
options.example: A squad considers reaching cover with two extra MF before it spends its first MF.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Declare Assault Movement
options.prompt: Can the planned move qualify for Assault Movement?
checks: Declare before moving; satisfy the one-Location and less-than-all-MF conditions, including qualifying bonuses and exclusions.
Do not apply it to Cavalry or prohibited PRC/hazardous activity. It cannot be voluntarily cancelled to recover options.
Avoiding FFNAM does not automatically avoid FFMO; reassess loss of status if the governing rules require it.
options.effect: Make the mode’s route constraints visible before commitment.
options.example: A one-Location move across Open Ground may avoid FFNAM while still receiving FFMO.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Declare Dash across a road
options.prompt: Does this road crossing qualify for Dash?
checks: Verify the declared start, crossed road Location and destination under A4.63 before accepting the mode.
Apply Dash-specific expenditure and defensive-fire restrictions rather than treating it as ordinary Assault Movement.
options.effect: Keep the crossing and its response opportunities linked as one special procedure.
options.example: The player compares an ordinary crossing with a qualifying Dash, without assuming every road hex permits one.

options.title: Declare Sewer entry
options.prompt: Should this unit use the Sewer route?
checks: Verify entry Location, unit and scenario qualifications.
Queue travel/Lost checks and a separate end-of-unit emergence attempt; ordinary surface routes do not describe this movement.
options.effect: Keep sewer position private as the rules require.
options.example: A sewer-moving stack has its emergence review at 3.41A even if its surface move list is empty.

options.title: Declare Climbing
options.prompt: Is Climbing the intended way across this cliff?
checks: Check unit eligibility, the cliff route and required declaration before movement.
Track Climb counters, costs and possible Falling checks through the procedure.
options.effect: Replace ordinary hex-entry prompts with climbing progress and exposure.
options.example: A climber’s partially completed ascent is not represented as an ordinary move into the upper hex.

options.title: Declare Human Wave or Banzai movement
options.prompt: Does this group qualify for the intended charge procedure?
checks: Validate participants, leadership, target/direction and nationality-specific declaration requirements.
Track each impulse and its constraints; expend the group’s MF/MP before First Fire.
Keep Japanese Banzai and other Human Wave variants distinct rather than copying one generic rule.
options.effect: Create one group procedure with individual casualties and movement states.
options.example: Several squads participate in a charge; resolving one squad’s fire result does not finish the other participants.

options.title: Declare Dare-Death berserk status
options.prompt: Should eligible Dare-Death Infantry become berserk now?
checks: Verify the designated unit and declaration conditions.
Once declared, follow the required charge in 3.32A rather than ordinary elective movement.
options.effect: Show the loss of route discretion before confirmation.
options.example: An eligible Chinese unit can choose the declaration, but cannot then choose an ordinary cautious route.

options.title: Declare Swimming movement
options.prompt: Can and should this unit cross by Swimming?
checks: Check water, unit, equipment and entry qualifications.
Queue required TC/MC, movement limitations and consequences instead of normal walking costs.
options.effect: Retain Swimming as a visible option even when water movement is not integrated.
options.example: The route includes water; the guide offers the rule reference without claiming the current engine can adjudicate it.

options.title: Declare Cavalry or wagon Gallop
options.prompt: Should the horse or wagon Gallop from the start?
checks: Check CX and type restrictions; opening Cavalry Gallop adds eight MF, wagon Gallop four.
Do not substitute the later Cavalry four-MF option for the opening declaration.
options.effect: Track mount and rider states separately where required.
options.example: A Cavalry unit weighs the opening eight-MF option before spending any movement.

options.title: Begin movement of a vehicle in Motion
options.prompt: Will this vehicle expend MP or MF now?
checks: Remove the Motion counter when the vehicle will expend movement as prescribed.
Preserve the correct Non-Stopped and moving-target conditions; removing the counter does not mean it Stopped.
options.effect: Keep separate fields for counter state, expenditure state and fire modifiers.
options.example: A vehicle begins ITS MPh from Motion without becoming a stationary firing target.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Check Column, Convoy and Platoon movement
options.prompt: Is movement linked to a formation?
checks: Validate formation membership, order and movement constraints before individual expenditure.
Track group expenditure, leaders and disbandment triggers; do not silently turn a group into independent moves.
options.effect: Expose each formation’s governing procedure and leave unavailable evaluators explicit.
options.example: A convoy member cannot skip ahead just because its individual MP budget allows it.

options.title: Attempt non-Platoon movement with a radioless AFV
options.prompt: Does this onboard AFV need permission to move independently?
checks: Check radioless status, Platoon choice and the Recalled exception.
Resolve the NTC and its consequences before normal movement; do not infer automatic success from an unimplemented check.
options.effect: Attach the roll to this vehicle’s movement instance.
options.example: An onboard radioless tank considers leaving its platoon; a Recalled vehicle uses the stated exception.

options.title: Declare a flail Trail Break attempt
options.prompt: Should the flail tank attempt a Trail Break in the minefield it will enter?
checks: Declare the attempt at the required opening window and identify the entry hex.
Apply flail capability, mine and path rules during movement; do not mark a safe route before resolution.
options.effect: Record the declared attempt separately from a successfully created TB.
options.example: Following units receive a usable route only after the flail procedure actually creates it.

options.title: Resolve opening Heavy Surf beaching checks
options.prompt: Does this boat or non-Aground LC require an opening (un)Beaching DR?
checks: Check craft state and Heavy Surf before normal movement.
Carry grounding, immobilization, broaching and swamping outcomes into later choices.
options.effect: A failed opening procedure can change which later actions remain available.
options.example: An LC cannot plan a normal landing while an unresolved opening surf result controls its state.

options.title: Enter or voluntarily abandon a vehicle
options.prompt: Should this unit enter the vehicle, or should its crew abandon it?
checks: Verify start-of-ITS-MPh position, all-MF cost, prior movement/fire and same-Player-Turn re-entry restrictions.
Offer permitted weapon removal and the abandoning inherent crew’s self-destruction/malfunction choice.
Resolve the associated fire window; entry and linked hooking succeed only if their survival conditions are met. Abandonment has its own outcome rules.
options.effect: Do not complete entry or hooking merely when MF are paid. Show the different commitments of entering and leaving.
options.example: A crew abandoning its vehicle considers removing an eligible weapon and wrecking the vehicle as it leaves.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Start the next aerial sequence
options.prompt: Have all ground movement sequences finished?
checks: Route an aerial glider to 3.37D before Evasive Action or landing.
If there is no aerial glider, use the all-parachute drift procedure at 3.34A; do not process parachutes as ordinary individual ground moves.
options.effect: Use a dedicated aerial sequence rather than the ground-unit expenditure loop.
options.example: The first glider receives its defender AA window before the landing attempt.

options.title: Conduct the required charge
options.prompt: What must this berserk unit do at its next expenditure?
checks: Apply charge target, route and entry restrictions, including relevant beach exceptions.
After each qualifying expenditure resolve 3.35D and 3.36D; berserk status does not bypass defensive fire.
options.effect: Reevaluate the charge after results instead of executing the whole plotted path at once.
options.example: A charge pauses for fire; surviving units continue according to their updated state.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Choose route, Location and cost
options.prompt: Which legal route and expenditure should be committed next?
checks: Calculate actual terrain, elevation, hexside, road, portage and movement-type costs. A road-rate entry can change exposure and TEM.
Distinguish Location changes from hex changes. Include bridges, gullies, streams, shellholes, crags, railroads and building levels in the full design.
Display pending terrain rules as not evaluated, not impassable; hidden obstacles must be adjudicated without advance disclosure.
options.effect: The completed Rules implementation supplies costs and exposure; the component explains the resulting choices.
options.example: A squad can compare a road-rate entry with entry through woods, including the different defensive-fire treatment.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Consider a Minimum Move
options.prompt: Can this Infantry make a one-hex Minimum Move?
checks: Retain at least one MF after excess portage deductions and satisfy the rule’s exclusions, including pushing a Gun or loading/unloading.
After entry and all First Fire, unbroken survivors become pinned and CX. Do not apply those states before the fire sequence.
options.effect: Show both the reachable hex and the resulting Pin/CX commitment.
options.example: A unit lacking the full entry cost may still qualify, but the move does not leave it ready for unrestricted follow-on action.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Choose Infantry Bypass or VBM
options.prompt: Is there sufficient clearance, and which side of the obstacle is being bypassed?
checks: Use unit-specific clearance, terrain and entry restrictions. Infantry and vehicle Bypass are not interchangeable.
Preserve route vertices/hexsides and facing for LOS and attacks, including applicable mine and SMOKE effects.
Do not allow an ordinary voluntary Infantry end in Bypass; handle the specific broken-unit and vehicle ending rules.
options.effect: Expose route geometry without presenting an unavailable LOS evaluator as a safe route.
options.example: Two routes through one woods hex may create different firing opportunities even though the destination hex is the same.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Review special terrain and fortification movement
options.prompt: Does this route require a special terrain procedure?
checks: Include tunnels, cliffs, Crest status, water/ice, rowhouses, Factories, fortified buildings, entrenchments, Wire, mines, pillboxes and roadblocks.
Include desert terrain, jungle, bamboo, huts, kunai, rice paddies, Panji and caves as explicit pending families; use scenario and equipment overlays.
Select the exact rule before committing. This family record is an index to detailed route rules, not evidence that every subcase has been adjudicated.
options.effect: Keep all named families discoverable; an unsupported cost needs an explanation and reference, not removal from the catalog.
options.example: A cave entry and a normal building entry both remain findable, but require different Rules projections.

options.title: Choose Start, Stop, Delay, Reverse or facing expenditure
options.prompt: What vehicle expenditure is intended now?
checks: Price each Start, Stop, Delay, Reverse, facing and route action under the applicable rule.
Give the defender each appropriate expenditure window before the next action; do not combine Stop and unload to suppress a response.
Track remaining MP and the consequences of ending movement, including assumed expenditures where required.
options.effect: The movement ledger must describe expenditures, not just a line of visited hexes.
options.example: A tank Stops before unloading; the defender’s Stop-MP response occurs before unloading is announced.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Resolve Mechanical Reliability, Stall and Bog Removal
options.prompt: Does this movement need a prerequisite check?
checks: Check vehicle-specific Mechanical Reliability/Stall triggers and Bog Removal conditions before continuation.
Keep Bog Removal distinct from a new terrain-entry Bog check; include LC Aground procedures where applicable.
options.effect: A failed check changes capability and stops stale route execution.
options.example: A Bogged vehicle cannot spend an ordinary movement entry while its removal result is unresolved.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Resolve sewer travel and Lost results
options.prompt: Has this sewer move reached a required roll?
checks: Perform Sewer dr and any required Lost dr at their prescribed timing.
Update the actual route privately and preserve the separate emergence procedure.
options.effect: Do not expose the concealed sewer route through counts or warnings.
options.example: A failed route result cannot be replaced by clicking the intended destination again.

options.title: Resolve Falling, Climb progress and Swimming checks
options.prompt: What consequences does this special movement trigger?
checks: Resolve any Falling DR and place the correct Climb counter after a successful ascent/descent.
Resolve required Swimming TC/MC; distinguish movement completion from surviving its checks.
options.effect: Keep required effects attached to their originating expenditure.
options.example: A successful climb changes the progress counter, while a Falling result requires resolution before another move.

options.title: Declare Double Time after starting
options.prompt: Would one additional MF help now?
checks: Verify that a late declaration remains legal for this unit and movement mode.
Gain one MF, not the opening two, and apply CX without undoing previous expenditures.
options.effect: Refresh remaining options and later-phase consequences.
options.example: A squad one MF short of its revised destination considers late Double Time.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Resolve concealment, detection and occupied entry
options.prompt: Does this expenditure require concealment or entry adjudication?
checks: Use the viewing side’s lawful information and the proper concealed/HIP reveal procedure.
Preserve voluntary choices where rules allow them, and handle forced-back or Infantry OVR branches at the correct point.
Resolve required PAATC and vehicle-ending detection separately; do not expose a hidden defender through route warnings.
options.effect: The UI receives only the disclosed outcome, not an omniscient eligibility list.
options.example: An attempted entry reveals a concealed SMC; the resulting OVR decision is handled before normal movement resumes.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Claim or relinquish Wall Advantage when allowed
options.prompt: Should this unit claim Wall Advantage at this point?
checks: Check claim timing, competing enemy claims and mandatory WA conditions.
Respect firing, movement and loss/reclaim restrictions; do not make WA a freely reversible display toggle.
options.effect: Update protection and related fire choices only after the legal state change.
options.example: A unit reaching a wall reviews its claim while the expenditure and opposing position are current.

options.title: Recover a SW or Gun
options.prompt: Should this unit spend movement to attempt Recovery?
checks: Check possession, Location, required MF and Recovery conditions; a failed attempt still has its prescribed expenditure.
Resolve the associated response window and any Ski-use dr. Update portage without refunding spent MF.
options.effect: Give each Recovery its own expenditure identity.
options.example: The squad enters a hex, survives the entry response, then attempts to Recover the abandoned LMG.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Drop a weapon or release prisoners
options.prompt: What should be left at this Location?
checks: Distinguish dropping a SW/Gun from releasing prisoners and follow the applicable ownership/guard rules.
Do not refund already lost movement allowance when dropping excess portage during the move.

Source tension: ASOP 3.32A lists dropping prisoners, while A20.53 sends voluntary abandonment to A20.5, which lists friendly RPh/APh. Keep the listed option visible, but require a resolved rule interpretation before enabling MPh abandonment.
options.effect: Leave an explicit position and possession record. Do not infer executable permission from this unresolved source tension.
options.example: Dropping a heavy weapon mid-route does not erase the cost already paid for carrying it.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Move Guards and prisoners, or escort prisoners offboard
options.prompt: How must the Guard and prisoners move together?
checks: Move prisoners as one combined stack at their Guard’s foot rate under the captor’s direction. Apply guarding capacity, weapon-use and transport capacity restrictions.
Consider a legal Friendly Board Edge escort exit and its victory-condition treatment; an ordinary edge is not automatically Friendly.
Resolve fire against both Guards and prisoners using the special casualty/Pin rules, and handle replacement Guards or freed Unarmed units when a Guard is eliminated.
options.effect: Track Guard identity and prisoner capacity through movement and casualties.
options.example: Mounted transport must have room for the prisoners as well as the Guard; a spare seat for the Guard alone is insufficient.

options.title: Enter an Unarmed unit’s Location to recapture it
options.prompt: Should eligible Infantry or Cavalry enter to attempt recapture?
checks: Unarmed units do not bar movement; entering Infantry/Cavalry can engage them in immediate CC during the MPh.
If the entry attack fails to eliminate or recapture them, place Melee and allow no further movement. This is neither ordinary Infantry OVR nor a free capture.
options.effect: Open the immediate combat consequence before continuing the route.
options.example: A squad enters a freed Unarmed unit’s hex; an unsuccessful recapture leaves the units in Melee.

options.title: Manhandle a Gun or boat
options.prompt: Can the crew or Personnel move this equipment by hand?
checks: Check pushing eligibility, route and modifiers; do not assume ordinary Infantry entry eligibility is sufficient.
Resolve Manhandling DR, TI and Labor on failure as prescribed, including the applicable defensive-fire exposure.
options.effect: Track the equipment and pushing units as a linked action.
options.example: A crew considers pushing its Gun into cover; a failed attempt still creates the relevant commitments.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Place a demolition charge
options.prompt: Can the carrier operably Place the DC and survive the response?
checks: Check ADJACENT target, LOS, movement/fire restrictions and any PAATC. Pay the placement MF in the carrier’s Location.
The carrier must survive the relevant defensive fire unbroken and unpinned for operable Placement.
A successfully Placed DC waits for its AFPh resolution; it does not explode merely because placement MF were spent.
options.effect: Track declared, operably Placed and detonated as different states.
options.example: A squad Places from cover. If pinned during the placement response, the DC is not operably Placed.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Set a demolition charge
options.prompt: Should the unit Set this DC for later use?
checks: Spend all MF using Hazardous Movement to Set it in the unit’s own Location; resolve the dr against the unit’s US#, with permitted assisting-leader drm.
The unit must avoid Pin/break for successful setting. Retain setting-unit identity and the later-Player-Turn, distance, LOS and NTC conditions for detonation.
options.effect: Create the later-use record without performing its eventual detonation.
options.example: A Set DC is not scheduled to explode automatically with an ordinary Placed DC in AFPh.

options.title: Mount, load, dismount or unload
options.prompt: Which transport change is intended, and who pays movement?
checks: Validate horse, vehicle, wagon, motorcycle or LC capacity, passenger/rider type, Location and movement state.
Account for both transport and Personnel expenditure and exposure. Resolve the loading/unloading survival rules.
Calculate remaining movement and fire restrictions from the transport-specific rule, not a generic four-MF reset.
options.effect: Show both participants and their remaining capabilities.
options.example: An unloading squad and its transport may have different remaining movement and fire options.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Hook or unhook a Gun
options.prompt: Should the Gun be attached to or removed from its towing vehicle?
checks: Check towing capability and legal Personnel/vehicle positions, then the linked expenditure and response.
Hooking makes Gun, Personnel and vehicle TI; unhooking makes Gun and Infantry TI under the cited procedure.
Honor survival requirements for simultaneous crew entry/exit and hooking; towing route restrictions continue afterward.
options.effect: Use a linked action record rather than changing only the Gun’s displayed carrier.
options.example: A crew abandoning its vehicle while unhooking must satisfy the relevant fire-survival conditions.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Declare Clearance work
options.prompt: Should this unit commit to Clearance?
checks: Represent rubble, Wire, mines, Set DC, roadblock, Path, Panji covered hexside and non-Factory Debris as separate selectable targets.
Apply TI and the target-specific declaration and later-resolution procedure. Do not remove the obstacle on declaration.
O1.5 is a named external-source gap in this volume; its detailed Debris conditions remain unevaluated.
options.effect: Create a pending work item linked to its actual resolution window.
options.example: A squad declares Wire Clearance now; the wire remains until the clearance procedure succeeds.

options.title: Attempt to extinguish Flame
options.prompt: Can this unit attempt Flame Clearance now?
checks: Check unit, Location and Flame conditions, then resolve the attempt.

Apply TI and task-specific Labor if unsuccessful. A Final Fire Clearance DR of 3-6 Hampers the Flame: mark it PIN so it cannot become Blaze during this Player Turn. A new Flame also uses PIN, but has a different origin. This immediate attempt is distinct from non-Flame work declared for CCPh.
options.effect: Show extinguished, Hampered, or still-active Flame, and carry the correct conversion eligibility into AFPh. Consideration does not resolve the task.
options.example: A failed attempt leaves a Labor counter and a still-present Flame.

options.title: Don or remove skis
options.prompt: Should this unit change ski use?
checks: Check the timing, movement cost and unit conditions in E4.2.
Carry ski status into movement, Recovery and combat effects; perform the Recovery-related Ski-use dr when called for.
options.effect: Keep equipment state and movement state linked.
options.example: A unit changes ski use for the next terrain segment rather than receiving ordinary walking costs automatically.

options.title: Place Smoke grenades or use a dispenser
options.prompt: Would Smoke help, and can this unit attempt it now?
checks: Separate Infantry grenades, vehicle grenades and dispenser types, including their usage limits and expenditure.
Resolve the usage result before assuming a Hindrance; apply WP NMC and possible Flame when triggered.
A failed attempt still follows its own cost and usage rules. Later smoke does not undo an earlier fire opportunity.
options.effect: Place smoke only after successful resolution and refresh subsequent LOS/exposure.
options.example: A squad attempts Smoke before crossing; the guide does not promise a protected crossing before the roll.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Attempt Infantry Overrun
options.prompt: Is this an eligible Infantry OVR situation?
checks: Use the Infantry target, unit, NTC and entry conditions, not the vehicular OVR procedure.
Handle concealed reveals, additional defenders and resulting forced-back or continuation decisions in source order.
options.effect: Keep the initial move, check and resulting entry branch traceable.
options.example: A lone enemy SMC may create an Infantry OVR choice that a normal occupied-entry rule would otherwise reject.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Create a Tank-Hunter or DC Hero
options.prompt: Can this Japanese squad or HS create the special hero now?
checks: For the movement attempt, verify the enemy AFV in LOS within eight MF and the governing creation restrictions.
Distinguish DC Hero conditions, equipment and compulsory follow-up from ordinary Tank-Hunter Hero creation.
options.effect: Queue the created hero’s procedure instead of granting generic hero movement.
options.example: A Japanese squad considers the attempt against a visible nearby tank; the reference remains present even when unimplemented.

options.title: Declare a late Gallop or Cavalry Charge
options.prompt: Should the Cavalry accelerate or commit to a Charge?
checks: A legal later Gallop adds four MF and requires the horse not be CX.
Declare a Charge while at least three hexes away and in LOS of its target; resolve the charge in the target Location.
options.effect: Keep Gallop and Charge as distinct choices with linked restrictions.
options.example: A rider cannot wait until adjacent to announce the Charge option listed for three or more hexes away.

options.title: Resolve entry Bog checks
options.prompt: Does the terrain entry or maneuver require Bog?
checks: Apply vehicle, terrain and entry modifiers at the prescribed point.
Update Bog/immobilization and any already-declared attack procedure before offering more movement.
options.effect: Do not discard a declared OVR merely because a Bog result occurred; use the OVR consequences.
options.example: A tank declaring an OVR into difficult terrain must settle Bog before resolving that attack.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Attempt the required Recall exit
options.prompt: Does Recall require this vehicle to leave?
checks: Use the Recall route and movement obligations rather than offering unrestricted tactical movement.
Include landing-craft exceptions and any inability to move or exit under the governing rules.
options.effect: Show the required exit task and its current impediments.
options.example: A Recalled vehicle is not treated as an optional unmoved unit at phase end.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Use Bounding First Fire
options.prompt: Should this vehicle fire now or retain its movement/fire choices?
checks: Check weapon and PRC eligibility, movement status, CA, ammunition, acquisition and applicable bounding-fire modifiers.
Track each weapon’s use, ROF and later-fire commitment; include C8.6 Smoke/WP timing exceptions.
Resolve results and any required consequences before continuing movement.
options.effect: Keep an attack tied to the current expenditure state rather than ending the vehicle’s move automatically.
options.example: A tank pauses to fire its MA, then checks whether movement and any additional weapon use remain legal.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Consider a Gun Duel response
options.prompt: Can this vehicle resolve an eligible shot before the declared defender attack?
checks: The declared opponent must satisfy the rule’s non-concealed, non-aerial conditions; check CA and fire eligibility.
Compare the required Gun Duel modifiers and honor the OVR exclusion; do not offer a generic interrupt against every shot.
options.effect: Resolve attack order through Rules, preserving the initiating defender attack if still applicable.
options.example: A tank named as a DFF target considers a legal BFF Gun Duel before the defender rolls.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Declare and resolve a vehicular Overrun
options.prompt: Should the vehicle Overrun this Location?
checks: Declare at entry as required; combine entry MP with the OVR cost of one quarter printed MP, rounded up, subject to exceptions.
Resolve applicable Bog and ordinary DFF before the OVR, then Reaction Fire after it. The OVR vehicle cannot invoke a Gun Duel.
Immobilization or destruction does not automatically cancel the OVR; use the applicable reduced attack and PRC consequences.
options.effect: Display the distinct before-OVR and after-OVR windows.
options.example: A defender’s shot immobilizes the attacking tank; the guide still resolves the OVR consequences that the rules require.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Attempt ESB or a Hull Down maneuver
options.prompt: Is extra speed or a Hull Down position worth the commitment?
checks: Present ESB and HD as separate actions, with their eligibility, MP and roll requirements.
Resolve breakdown or maneuver failure before calculating subsequent capability; nationality and vehicle data matter.
options.effect: Preview the cost and possible movement loss without inventing success probabilities.
options.example: A tank short of its intended destination can consider ESB, while a different position may permit an HD maneuver.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Change CE or BU posture
options.prompt: Can the crew change posture at this exact moment?
checks: Do not both voluntarily place and remove CE in the same phase.
Do not change after the vehicle/PRC’s Prep or Bounding First Fire, or between being named a target and resolution of all fire allowed by the last MP expenditure.
Apply linked passenger and crew exceptions; the posture change alone is not movement for moving-target/firer penalties.
options.effect: Expose the timing restriction before a shot rather than allowing a reactive BU toggle after target declaration.
options.example: A CE tank named as a target cannot become BU while the current fire window remains unresolved.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Move Infantry with an AFV in Armored Assault
options.prompt: Should the Infantry and AFV move together?
checks: Begin with the Infantry beneath the AFV and apply the combined movement requirements.
Limit how far the AFV may move by the accompanying Infantry’s movement potential even if they later separate.
Apply protection to the actual combined move; it does not eliminate FFNAM unless Assault Movement applies.
options.effect: Track a shared route segment and independent consequences after separation.
options.example: The squad leaves the tank to enter a building; the tank’s remaining route still respects the Armored Assault distance constraint.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Declare Wreck Removal
options.prompt: Can this vehicle undertake Wreck Removal?
checks: Check the vehicle, wreck, location and commitment required by D10.42.
Record the declaration now and resolve the result at 3.51A, rather than deleting the wreck immediately.
options.effect: Maintain a pending phase-end work item.
options.example: The wreck remains on the map while the declared removal procedure awaits its proper resolution.

options.title: Resolve wagon or motorcycle Wreck Checks
options.prompt: Has this movement triggered a Wreck Check?
checks: Use the specific wagon or motorcycle trigger and modifiers.
Resolve the check and its passenger/equipment consequences before continuing.
options.effect: Do not substitute a tank Bog check for these different procedures.
options.example: A motorcycle’s hazardous movement segment may call for its own Wreck Check.

options.title: Complete the impulse before First Fire
options.prompt: Have all participating units made this impulse’s expenditures?
checks: Commit the prescribed group expenditures before the defensive-fire procedure.
Preserve each participant’s cost, position and eligibility when resolving attacks and consequences.
options.effect: The response window identifies the impulse as well as the affected target.
options.example: The defender cannot interrupt halfway through a group’s required simultaneous expenditure by using ordinary single-unit sequencing.

options.title: Check Column Disbandment
options.prompt: Has movement or fire triggered Column Disbandment?
checks: Check the movement triggers at 3.32A and the residual/fire triggers at 3.35D and 3.36D.
Carry the changed formation and movement state into subsequent expenditure choices.
options.effect: One acknowledgment cannot clear later independent disbandment triggers.
options.example: The column remains intact after one move, but a later attack creates a new check.

options.title: Resolve a Panji movement MC
options.prompt: Does this entry or crossing trigger Panji effects?
checks: Use the actual Panji terrain and movement conditions.
Resolve the MC and resulting state before further movement; preserve hidden obstacle disclosure rules.
options.effect: Show an encountered effect only when its disclosure is authorized.
options.example: The UI must not warn about an undiscovered Panji feature before the normal encounter procedure.

options.title: Create Vehicle Dust when required
options.prompt: Does this vehicle expenditure create Dust?
checks: Check the applicable desert/environmental conditions and vehicle movement.
Place and update dust by its rule, then reevaluate subsequent LOS and Hindrances.
options.effect: Dust is an expenditure consequence, not an optional cosmetic trail.
options.example: The tank’s movement may change a later shot’s visibility even if no smoke was fired.

options.title: Drop DD tank screens
options.prompt: Should the DD tank lower its screens now?
checks: Check the permitted conditions and resulting movement/fire restrictions.
Record the configuration change with its rule consequences rather than treating it as CE/BU.
options.effect: Keep screen state distinct from crew posture.
options.example: An amphibious tank reaching the landing area reviews its DD configuration.

options.title: Beach, unbeach or resolve Aground
options.prompt: What landing or departure procedure applies here?
checks: Separate boats from LC and legal Beach/Unbeach choices from required Aground checks.
Use the current beach, water, tide and craft state; include corresponding transport restrictions.
options.effect: A beached, aground or mobile craft has different next choices.
options.example: An LC that runs Aground cannot continue as though it merely paid an ordinary entry cost.

options.title: Resolve Swamping, Heavy Surf and Wading CX
options.prompt: Which surf effects follow this expenditure?
checks: Resolve applicable Swamping, Immobilization, (un)Beaching and Broaching effects.
Infantry/Cavalry Wading in Heavy Surf become CX as prescribed. Keep the craft and its contents’ outcomes linked.
options.effect: Carry the new state into fire, transport and remaining movement decisions.
options.example: Troops Wading in Heavy Surf acquire CX even without choosing Double Time.

options.title: Take required glider Evasive Action
options.prompt: Does the last AA result require Evasive Action?
checks: Resolve the required action and resulting aerial position.
Return to 3.37D for the next applicable AA opportunity; do not proceed directly to landing after every shot.
options.effect: Represent the glider’s repeated AA/evasion sequence explicitly.
options.example: An AA result changes the landing approach and creates the next source-defined aerial window.

options.title: Drift all aerial parachutes
options.prompt: Where do all remaining aerial parachutes drift?
checks: Apply the drift procedure to all aerial parachutes before the 3.38D fire step.
If none remain aerial, proceed to phase-end work; do not invent a ground MF expenditure.
options.effect: Keep aerial position and later landing displacement separate.
options.example: All parachutes drift before the defender chooses eligible fire at them.

options.title: Resolve existing Residual FP and Fire Lanes
options.prompt: Does this expenditure trigger an existing residual attack?
checks: Resolve applicable existing residual before new DFF, against the moving unit/stack only.
Apply the once-per-Location and increased-vulnerability/strength exceptions; a multi-MF expenditure is not automatically multiple residual attacks.
Use separate Fire Lane rules and applicable activity/entry timing exceptions.
options.effect: Keep a per-target exposure record, not a simple once-per-hex checkbox.
options.example: A unit already attacked by residual may face another qualifying attack after its vulnerability increases and it spends more MF.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Resolve FFE attacks on moving units
options.prompt: Does the current move trigger an existing FFE effect?
checks: Use the FFE type, expenditure and location rules; include WP, rockets, LC and NOBA/Reverse Slope exceptions.
Attack the qualifying moving unit/stack, not every stationary unit sharing the Location on each expenditure.
options.effect: This resolves an existing mission’s effect; it is not an unrestricted new OBA mission window.
options.example: A moving squad enters an FFE area while a stationary squad is already there; their exposure histories are distinct.

options.title: Resolve minefield attacks
options.prompt: Has the expenditure triggered a mine attack?
checks: Apply AP/AT mine, entry/exit, known route and clearance/TB exceptions as appropriate.
Disclose mine information only through the rule’s encounter procedure; do not expose hidden fields in route suggestions.
options.effect: Attach the attack and discovered information to this movement event.
options.example: The player sees a mine attack when it occurs, not an advance warning based on hidden scenario data.

options.title: Attempt later defender illumination
options.prompt: Is a later Starshell attempt permitted now?
checks: Check leader eligibility and the special MMC/CE AFV condition when a Starshell/IR has been fired in no previous Player Turn.
Resolve illumination before subsequent attacks that use the changed visibility.
options.effect: Do not carry the broader opening opportunity into every later response without checking its conditions.
options.example: A later movement expenditure may offer a leader a Starshell attempt without giving every MMC the same right.

options.title: Resolve trip-flare activation
options.prompt: Does the move activate a trip flare?
checks: Check the triggering condition and resolve the resulting illumination and disclosure.
Keep this automatic effect distinct from an optional Starshell attempt.
options.effect: Refresh the current response’s visibility after activation.
options.example: The defender’s possible fire changes after the movement activates illumination.

options.title: Fire at the current expenditure, or pass
options.prompt: Should this defender fire at the current mover now?
checks: Target only the qualifying moving unit/stack, using its route, expenditure and state. A stationary co-occupant is not automatically a target.
Limit repeated shots by MF/MP expenditure even when ROF is retained; a one-MF expenditure is not unlimited fire.
Apply range, LOS, weapon use, fire-group, leadership, cowering and ammunition rules. Passing this window does not pass later ones.
options.effect: Keep the shot allowance for this expenditure separate from remaining weapon capability.
options.example: A retained-ROF MG may still have to wait for a later expenditure before firing again at this mover.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Use Subsequent First Fire
options.prompt: Can this First-Fired unit use SFF against the mover?
checks: Check eligible small-arms/MG/IFE use, Normal Range and the nearest Known armed enemy distance restriction.
Apply Area Fire and relevant Sustained Fire rules; use or forfeit the usable MG/IFE capability as A8.3 requires.
Place Final Fire markers on the unit and its weapons appropriately.
options.effect: Show what this choice gives up for later defensive opportunities.
options.example: A First-Fired squad cannot use SFF at a farther target merely because that target is moving.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Use Final Protective Fire
options.prompt: Is the adjacent or same-hex mover worth another FPF attack?
checks: Check Final-Fired Infantry, target and weapon restrictions; apply the required inherent and MG/IFE use.
Resolve the attack and use the same Original IFT DR as the firer’s NMC under the rule’s leadership conditions.
The target’s attack result is not cancelled if the firer breaks. Further FPF requires continued eligibility and available expenditure opportunity.
options.effect: Link the defender’s morale consequence to the attack record.
options.example: A squad’s FPF breaks the moving enemy but also breaks the firing squad; both outcomes remain.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Resolve mandatory same-Location fire
options.prompt: Does enemy Infantry/Cavalry entry compel an attack?
checks: After residual, mines and OBA, evaluate unbroken armed Infantry not in Melee and the entering MMC conditions.
Apply compulsory fire-group and weapon-use rules with their exceptions; this is not an optional Pass window.
options.effect: A required-fire obligation blocks closing the response until resolved.
options.example: A qualifying MMC enters the defender’s Location; the guide replaces a generic optional-fire prompt with the mandatory procedure.

options.title: Take a Snap Shot
options.prompt: Does the crossed hexside present a legal Snap Shot?
checks: Require LOS to the entire crossed hexside and eligible small-arms/MG use; exclude ordnance, IFE, Canister and prohibited MG CA changes.
Apply Area Fire without FFNAM/FFMO, limit it to the qualifying crossing opportunity, and leave no Residual FP.
options.effect: Store the crossing geometry so the opportunity cannot be recreated after movement has advanced.
options.example: A defender sees the crossed hexside but not the destination center, creating a possible Snap Shot.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Establish or maintain a Fire Lane
options.prompt: Would a legal Fire Lane cover useful later movement?
checks: Check the MG, initial attack, lane geometry and LOS conditions before placement.
Apply Fire Lane attacks and cancellation independently from ordinary Residual FP, including any cancellation from CC Reaction Fire.
options.effect: Show the lane’s future coverage without claiming guaranteed targets.
options.example: A defender trades the relevant MG capability for a lane that may affect later movers.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Review eligible weapons and attack modes
options.prompt: Which legal weapon and attack mode fits this response?
checks: Include inherent fire, MG, FT, MOL, LATW, ordnance/IFE, permitted special ammunition, Spraying Fire and fire-group/direction choices.
Apply actual first/subsequent/final-fire and target restrictions; Intensive Fire is not a blanket right for every weapon or response.
Recheck ROF, malfunctions, acquisition, ammo depletion and result chains for each shot, including cave and equipment-note exceptions.
options.effect: Reuse shared firing definitions from Prep Fire, with MPh-specific eligibility instead of copied permission rules.
options.example: A Gun and a squad in one Location may have different legal responses to the same MP expenditure.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Throw a DC during defensive fire
options.prompt: Is a Thrown DC attack permitted against this mover?
checks: Check range, LOS, unit/weapon-use and timing conditions. A unit already marked First Fire cannot Throw a DC, and it cannot do so as SFF or FPF.
Resolve both target and throwing-Location consequences under the Thrown DC procedure; do not treat it as a Placed DC waiting for AFPh.
options.effect: The checklist warns of consequences to the thrower before committing.
options.example: The defender considers a DC against a nearby mover while accounting for the attack on the throwing Location.

options.title: Fire an OVR Prevention shot
options.prompt: Can this non-vehicular Gun take an OVR Prevention shot?
checks: Check the Gun’s CA, current fire markers and No IF restriction immediately after the OVR expenditure is announced, before the OVR resolves.
The Original TH DR also tests its manning Infantry. Pin or break voids the TH attempt except for specified malfunction/Low Ammo effects.
Apply IF penalties and No Fire afterward where required. An otherwise unfired Gun uses the C5.641 exceptions; do not apply the same penalty and marker to every case.
options.effect: Show the risk to the crew and the possibility that its shot is voided before commitment.
options.example: A Gun that already Intensive Fired may have this final qualifying defense, but a failed crew check can leave the OVR unaffected.

options.title: Resolve CC or non-CC Reaction Fire
options.prompt: Which response to this vehicle is legal at this point?
checks: Separate ordinary DFF before an OVR from Reaction Fire after it, and distinguish CC from non-CC procedures.
Evaluate PAATC, Street Fighting, fire-marker and weapon conditions under the relevant rule.
Include the separate OVR Prevention procedure of C5.64 where applicable, rather than treating it as unrestricted FPF.
options.effect: A vehicle attack can open more than one differently timed response window.
options.example: A unit considers a legal CC Reaction Fire attack after the OVR resolves, not as a substitute for pre-OVR DFF.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Create a Tank-Hunter Hero in a CC Reaction Fire position
options.prompt: Can this Japanese squad or HS attempt hero creation here?
checks: Verify the CC Reaction Fire position and relevant creation conditions.
Use the defender timing and follow-up procedure rather than copying the attacker’s movement creation window.
options.effect: Keep this defender option present even when special nationality rules are pending.
options.example: An approaching AFV creates a qualifying reaction position for a Japanese squad.

options.title: Attempt defender Motion or a Smoke Dispenser response
options.prompt: Can this vehicle react without waiting for its own MPh?
checks: Check the specific Motion attempt conditions, expenditure basis and limits; it is not a general move-away action.
Evaluate dispenser eligibility and timing independently, then apply usage and resulting smoke effects.
options.effect: Motion and dispenser choices remain separate actions within the current response window.
options.example: A defending tank may consider Motion or smoke against the mover without gaining an ordinary movement turn.

options.title: Conduct Sighting TC and Ground Support
options.prompt: Can available aircraft attack this moving target?
checks: Check sighting, target, attack and nationality/scenario restrictions; do not treat aircraft as an ordinary ground DFF weapon.
Open the attacker’s appropriate Light AA response and resolve attack results/markers in source order.
Apply Chapter W restrictions where relevant, including consecutive-Player-Turn Ground Support limits; FAC-directed PFPh CAS is a different window.
options.effect: Link aircraft attack and ground AA responses without changing the Player Turn roles.
options.example: The DEFENDER’s aircraft attacks, but the ATTACKER may now have an AA decision.

options.title: Use Light AA against attacking aircraft
options.prompt: Which eligible weapons may answer this air attack?
checks: Check Light AA weapon, target and current commitments.
Apply AA/Prep/Bounding Fire or Gunflash markers as required, preserving subsequent movement and fire restrictions.
options.effect: Switch the displayed decision owner to ATTACKER for this window.
options.example: An attacker’s weapon answers a diving aircraft while the defender’s ground-fire sequence is temporarily interrupted.

options.title: Place residual and fire markers correctly
options.prompt: What persists after this attack?
checks: Use the residual half-FP calculation, reductions and cap in source order. Apply ordnance-hit and ammo/dud exceptions, not a blanket no-ordnance rule.
A malfunctioned weapon or Snap Shot leaves no ordinary residual; retained ROF and the immediate decision to forfeit it require their own accounting.
Place First/Final/Intensive/No Fire/Gunflash markers as required. Resolve MOL-Projector Smoke and possible Flame separately.
options.effect: Record residual and marker effects before reopening movement.
options.example: A MG retaining ROF needs the appropriate residual decision now, not after the next unit enters.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Fire Light AA at an aerial glider
options.prompt: Is Light AA fire available against this glider?
checks: Use the special First/Subsequent First Fire rules and required AA/fire/Gunflash markers.
After fire, go to Evasive Action at 3.33A; if no Light AA fire occurred, go to landing at 3.42A.
options.effect: Do not expose a ground-unit FPF menu for an aerial glider.
options.example: Declining eligible AA advances the glider toward landing rather than returning to ordinary ground movement.

options.title: Fire at aerial parachutes
options.prompt: Which parachutes and weapons qualify for fire?
checks: Use small arms or Light AA only, with the special First/Subsequent First Fire conditions.
Place required markers, then proceed to the collective landing procedure at 3.43A.
options.effect: Aerial target and weapon restrictions are visible before attack selection.
options.example: An otherwise available heavy weapon does not gain permission to fire at parachutes simply by appearing in the unit’s weapon list.

options.title: Consider Search before ending ITS MPh
options.prompt: Does this eligible unit have a useful Search opportunity?
checks: Check non-Bypassing Good Order Infantry/Cavalry and qualifying MMC/stack conditions, remaining one MF, Pin and Assault Movement exclusions.
Apply search area, dr modifiers, exclusions, own-hex search and authorized reveal results. Mine discovery does not automatically disclose type or strength.
Resolve possible Search casualties and night/Japanese exceptions. Search makes the unit TI, but its expenditure still permits DFF/SFF/FPF.
options.effect: End this move must offer the remaining Search choice without suggesting that undiscovered enemies exist.
options.example: A squad retains one MF and can Search adjacent accessible Locations. The response to that MF remains live.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Move broken Infantry from Bypass into the obstacle
options.prompt: Did Infantry break while in Bypass?
checks: At ITS MPh end apply the required obstacle entry procedure.
Preserve the resulting Location and subsequent rout obligations; do not leave the unit in an ordinary voluntary Bypass ending.
options.effect: This required transition is separate from optional end-of-move review.
options.example: A squad broken while bypassing woods enters the obstacle according to A4.32.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Attempt sewer emergence
options.prompt: Where can this sewer unit or stack emerge?
checks: Resolve the required emergence dr and the rule’s legal outcomes.
Disclose position and units only as the emergence procedure permits.
options.effect: Do not mark a sewer move complete while emergence remains unresolved.
options.example: The intended exit is a plan; the emergence result determines the actual outcome.

options.title: Scrounge small arms with an Unarmed unit
options.prompt: Can this Unarmed unit attempt to rearm here?
checks: Check all-MF-spent movement and terrain conditions, including non-water/non-marsh, and the once-per-hex-per-MPh limit.
Use the required DR and nationality-specific rearming outcome. This is not Rally wreck Scrounging.
options.effect: Preserve the hex attempt limit across different Unarmed units.
options.example: A second Unarmed unit cannot repeat an already-used hex attempt just because its own checklist is new.

options.title: End the vehicle’s move Stopped or in Motion
options.prompt: What is this vehicle’s legal end-of-move state?
checks: Place Motion on a qualifying vehicle or expend Stop MP as required.
Resolve any final expenditure responses and place a CC counter if necessary before selecting another mover.
options.effect: End this vehicle’s move does not end THE MPh.
options.example: Choosing to Stop creates its applicable MP response; a phase-end button cannot bypass it.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Resolve glider landing and possible crash
options.prompt: What landing result does this glider obtain?
checks: Resolve the Landing DR and any Crash dr using the actual approach and terrain.
Return to 3.23A after this glider’s sequence; defer contents placement to its specified later window, including AFPh E8.4.
options.effect: Do not unload all glider contents as ordinary MPh passengers.
options.example: The glider lands now, while the later placement of contents remains a distinct procedure.

options.title: Resolve collective parachute landing
options.prompt: Which landing displacement and checks apply?
checks: Move all non-German 5/8-inch parachutes one hex as prescribed, then land all parachutes and flip the 1/2-inch counters.
Resolve the required NMC/NTC and terrain outcomes before moving to phase-end procedures.
options.effect: Keep nationality and counter-size distinctions explicit.
options.example: German and non-German parachutes cannot be processed by one unconditional extra-hex rule.

options.title: Resolve required terrain-Blaze eliminations
options.prompt: Are affected vehicles or landed aerial units still in a terrain Blaze?
checks: Apply the vehicle-unable-to-leave and glider/parachute landing conditions.
Resolve elimination and associated contents consequences before completing THE MPh.
options.effect: This is a phase-end obligation, not an optional warning.
options.example: A landed glider in terrain Blaze requires its prescribed outcome even after all movement choices were considered.

options.title: Resolve declared Wreck Removal
options.prompt: Which declared Wreck Removal attempts are due?
checks: Resolve each valid declaration under its governing conditions.
Update wreck and vehicle state and retain failed outcomes; merely considering the topic did not create a declaration.
options.effect: Match each result to its earlier work item.
options.example: The guide resolves the vehicle’s previously declared attempt without repeating the declaration.

options.title: Locate pre-1942 German paratroop arms canisters
options.prompt: Are eligible air-dropped German MMC seeking arms canisters?
checks: Check the pre-1942, air-drop and unit conditions.
Use the specific canister-location procedure, not ordinary SW Recovery or Unarmed Scrounging.
options.effect: Keep this historical equipment option visible for the relevant scenario profile.
options.example: A qualifying paratroop scenario has a phase-end task that an ordinary Infantry scenario does not.

options.title: Return qualifying berserk units to Good Order
options.prompt: Do any berserk units have no Known enemy in LOS?
checks: Evaluate the actual phase-end condition under A15.46.
Do not confuse this return with the different later AFPh return condition after eliminating Known enemies.
options.effect: Update the unit before DFPh and preserve lawful information boundaries.
options.example: A berserk unit with no Known enemy in LOS is reviewed at this step, not at the end of each expenditure.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Remove Residual FP and half-inch SMOKE
options.prompt: Which counters expire at the end of THE MPh?
checks: Remove all residual, including Fire Lane residual, and the applicable 1/2-inch SMOKE counters.
Honor the cave exception and counter type; do not remove every SMOKE counter or all defensive fire markers.
options.effect: Clear only due effects, retaining First/Final Fire commitments for their later removal windows.
options.example: A First Fire marker remains for DFPh even after its residual counter is removed.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Resolve Jitter when triggered
options.prompt: Has a qualifying night procedure triggered Jitter?
checks: Use the trigger, Gunflash conditions, side/unit selection and eligible weapon restrictions in E1.55.
Jitter is not a freely chosen attack; apply the resulting movement/fire effects, including cancellation where required.
Chapter W bugles introduce their own night trigger and visibility treatment rather than ordinary voluntary Starshell fire.
options.effect: Interrupt the originating movement check and resume only after the night procedure settles.
options.example: A doubles Straying result can create a Jitter sequence instead of simply choosing a new route.
options.timing: Rule-specific MPh timing; supplemental to ASOP

options.title: Apply CPVA IPM and non-IPM movement rules
options.prompt: Must these CPVA units move as a group, or do they qualify for an exception?
checks: Apply squad/HS, Recon, leader-initiation and joining distinctions; preserve group connectivity and impulse rules.
For a required non-IPM NTC, apply exemptions, night modifier and failure movement/order consequences; do not trigger SAN or concealment loss from this check.
Handle newly berserk participants and broken connectivity through the Chapter W procedure. Apply W7.9 restrictions, including no Armored Assault and the specified Rider exceptions.
options.effect: Keep CPVA movement explicit rather than labelling it ordinary Platoon movement.
options.example: A failed non-IPM attempt may restrict a unit to one Location before other movement, rather than simply consuming a generic action.
options.timing: Rule-specific MPh timing; supplemental to ASOP

options.title: Use CPVA bugles when an SSR permits
options.prompt: Does this scenario permit the opening bugle choice?
checks: Check the SSR and eligible Good Order leader onboard or entering, at the start of the CPVA MPh.
Apply the Jitter/initial-illumination equivalence, CPVA non-IPM and concealment modifiers, and the UN Scenario Defender leader’s Freedom of Movement opportunity.

For the specified dates and UN nationalities, perform required Jitter-only Straying checks even in daytime or when an initial night Movement DR is unnecessary. Apply the stated unit-quality treatment and avoid a second Jitter trigger from a later Movement DR.
options.effect: Place the choice at phase start, not as a freely repeatable mid-move action.
options.example: A qualifying SSR adds an opening decision; without that SSR the reference remains visible as scenario-dependent.
options.timing: Rule-specific MPh timing; supplemental to ASOP

options.title: Declare an SSR-enabled UN Bayonet Charge
options.prompt: Does the scenario permit this designated UN Infantry to charge?
checks: Use the Banzai-derived procedure with W.6 exceptions, including Known enemy Infantry targeting and participant qualifications.
Apply leader/NTC nationality exceptions, failure movement and later Hand-to-Hand consequences; do not copy Japanese end-state rules unchanged.
options.effect: Show the declaration before movement and preserve its compulsory follow-through.
options.example: A designated UN squad’s failed qualifying check has the specified restricted movement outcome.
options.timing: Rule-specific MPh timing; supplemental to ASOP

options.title: Maintain or track Chapter W searchlights
options.prompt: Must the beam be maintained, tracked or cancelled?
checks: At the start of the enemy MPh resolve required maintenance/reliability; track a moving target only under the beam and LOS rules.
Check the limited moving-target exception for a new target within NVR and the conditions for cancellation.
Do not offer unrestricted beam retargeting or cancellation on every expenditure.
options.effect: Attach beam changes to the proper movement window and visibility projection.
options.example: A moving unit leaves the beam; the searchlight’s tracking rule determines whether the beam may follow.
options.timing: Rule-specific MPh timing; supplemental to ASOP

options.title: Resolve attack results, Snipers, wounds and forced movement
options.refs: A7-A8; A14; A15; A17; D5; ASOP dagger
options.prompt: Which required results remain from the last roll?
checks: Resolve morale, Pin, casualty, leader loss, HOB/berserk, wound, Stun/Recall, collateral and terrain effects when actually triggered.
Apply Sniper activation/check eligibility and exclusions to the originating roll; do not create one generic end-of-MPh Sniper task.
Recalculate ongoing movement after results, including interrupted impulses and charge obligations.
options.effect: A required consequence cannot be satisfied by marking this reference topic considered.
options.example: A wound changes remaining movement capability; the previously plotted route needs reevaluation.
options.status: Partially integrated; complete rule path remains to be verified.
options.timing: Rule-specific MPh timing; supplemental to ASOP

options.title: Apply scenario, equipment and external-module exceptions
options.refs: Chapter H notes; SSR; ASOP dagger; O1.5
options.prompt: Does this scenario or equipment introduce an additional MPh condition?
checks: Keep Chapter F/G/W and equipment-note options visible even though the current implementation passes focus on A-E.

glossary.MF: Movement Factors, used by Infantry and certain other movement types. Do not interchange with vehicle MP.
glossary.MP: Movement Points. Vehicle expenditure and the resulting defensive-fire opportunity are tracked separately from distance.
glossary.DFF: Defensive First Fire, attacks against eligible moving targets during the opponent’s MPh.
glossary.ITS MPh: The movement sequence of the current unit or stack, distinct from the entire Movement Phase.
glossary.MPh: Movement Phase. THE MPh contains a separate start, during and end for each moving unit or stack.
glossary.Human Wave: Group movement under A25.23 and applicable nationality rules, using ordered impulses.
glossary.LOS: Line of Sight. Guidance uses only information the viewing player may know.
glossary.NVR: Night Visibility Range, used with illumination and other night visibility exceptions.
glossary.CE: Crew Exposed. A vehicle crew posture whose voluntary changes have timing restrictions.
glossary.IR: Illuminating Round, with its own usage and placement procedure.
glossary.ILH: Intended Landing Hex for a glider.
glossary.TI: Task Involved status, not a synonym for Prep Fire.
glossary.CX: Counter Exhausted. A state caused by Double Time and other rules, with consequences beyond extra movement.
glossary.SW: Support Weapon. Using one affects its possessor’s capability accounting.
glossary.PP: Portage Points, the load represented by carried equipment.
glossary.IPC: Inherent Portage Capacity. Excess portage affects the moving unit’s available MF.
glossary.Freedom of Movement: Night Scenario Defender restriction and release procedure under E1.21, not ordinary movement eligibility.
glossary.NTC: Normal Task Check, used only when the governing rule calls for it.
glossary.Straying: A rules-driven departure from intended movement in specified night or terrain conditions.
glossary.DR: Two-dice roll. Keep Original, modified and individual colored/white values.
glossary.Double Time: An Infantry choice to gain MF and become CX. Declaration at the start and later in ITS MPh gives different bonuses.
glossary.Assault Movement: A declared Infantry movement mode under A4.61. It can avoid FFNAM without automatically avoiding FFMO.
glossary.FFNAM: First Fire Non-Assault Movement, a modifier tied to movement and activity, not merely a changed hex.
glossary.FFMO: First Fire Movement in Open Ground, assessed for the particular attack and route.
glossary.Dash: The special road-crossing movement procedure of A4.63, subject to its own declaration and route conditions.
glossary.Hazardous Movement: A defined exposure condition for specified activities, not a generic label for a dangerous route.
glossary.Banzai: The Japanese charge procedure derived from Human Wave rules with G1.5 exceptions.
glossary.Impulse: A coordinated expenditure by a qualifying group, completed for the group before the response procedure.
glossary.Motion: A vehicle state. It is not interchangeable with Non-Stopped or a moving target for fire modifiers.
glossary.Non-Stopped: Vehicle condition used in movement and firing rules. It is distinct from a Motion counter.
glossary.TB: Trail Break. Creation and use depend on terrain and the applicable vehicle procedure.
glossary.LC: Landing Craft, governed by its own transport, fire, beaching and grounding rules.
glossary.Minimum Move: A4.134 permits certain one-hex moves despite insufficient MF, with Pin and CX consequences after First Fire.
glossary.Bypass: Movement around a permitted obstacle within its hex. Clearance, costs and attack geometry depend on the unit and route.
glossary.VBM: Vehicular Bypass Movement. Uses vehicle-specific clearance, costs, facing and defensive-fire geometry.
glossary.VCA: Vehicular Covered Arc, the vehicle hull’s facing.
glossary.TCA: Turret Covered Arc, distinct from the vehicle hull’s covered arc.
glossary.WA: Wall Advantage. Its claim, loss and mandatory conditions depend on B9.32 and the position.
glossary.OVR: Overrun. Infantry OVR and vehicular OVR are different procedures with different prerequisites.
glossary.PAATC: Pre-AFV Attack Task Check, required in specified Infantry attacks or entries involving an AFV.
glossary.US#: Unit Size Number. Used for purposes including prisoner guarding capacity and the dr to Set a DC; it is not a weapon Usage Number.
glossary.PRC: Passengers, Riders and Crew, with different vulnerability and fire restrictions.
glossary.CC: Close Combat. A CC counter and MPh CC Reaction Fire have distinct timing from the later Close Combat Phase.
glossary.AFPh: Advancing Fire Phase. Opportunity Fire reserves a full-effect attack here.
glossary.SMOKE: The umbrella for Smoke and WP effects; preserve ammunition type, owner and source.
glossary.WP: White Phosphorus, with its own height, NMC and ignition rules.
glossary.T-H Hero: Tank-Hunter Hero, created and used under G1.42 rather than ordinary hero rules.
glossary.DC Hero: A Japanese hero using the special demolition-charge procedure of G1.424.
glossary.BFF: Bounding First Fire, eligible vehicular fire during the vehicle’s MPh.
glossary.ROF: Rate of Fire. A retained opportunity is not an automatic shot.
glossary.TH: To Hit roll or number for an ordnance attack.
glossary.Gun Duel: C2.2401 procedure that can alter which eligible declared attack resolves first.
glossary.Reaction Fire: Defender attacks against vehicles under D7.2, with separate CC and non-CC procedures.
glossary.ESB: Excessive Speed Breakdown. Extra vehicle movement is subject to the governing breakdown risk.
glossary.HD: Hull Down. A vehicle protection state, including a possible maneuver attempt under D4.22.
glossary.BU: Buttoned Up. The alternative protected crew posture, with weapon and observation consequences.
glossary.Wreck Check: A specified check for wagons or motorcycles in the circumstances of D12.4/D15.46.
glossary.DD: Duplex Drive tank. Its screens and amphibious state have specific consequences.
glossary.Residual FP: Firepower left by a qualifying attack, applied to later qualifying expenditures under A8.2.
glossary.Fire Lane: A machine-gun residual-fire procedure with its own placement, attack and cancellation rules.
glossary.FFE: Fire For Effect. FFE:1, FFE:2 and FFE:C have different actions.
glossary.SFF: Subsequent First Fire, restricted additional defensive fire after First Fire.
glossary.IFE: Infantry Firepower Equivalent, a weapon-specific alternative to ordinary TH fire.
glossary.Sustained Fire: Additional MG/IFE fire with its own firepower and breakdown consequences.
glossary.FPF: Final Protective Fire, restricted further fire that also tests the firer’s morale.
glossary.TPBF: Triple Point Blank Fire. Some same-Location entry attacks are compulsory under A8.312.
glossary.TK: To Kill resolution, distinct from the To Hit roll.
glossary.IF: Intensive Fire, an extra Gun shot with accuracy and malfunction penalties.
glossary.FB: Fighter-Bomber, an aircraft type with its own sighting and Ground Support procedures.
glossary.DB: Dive Bomber, an aircraft type with its own attack and AA response procedures.
glossary.MOL: Molotov Cocktail. A squad MOL and a MOL Projector have different procedures.
glossary.Search: An end-of-ITS-MPh procedure using a qualifying unit or stack. It is not a free inspection of hidden information.
glossary.MMC: Multi-Man Counter: squad, half-squad or crew.
glossary.Jitter: Night firing caused by the E1.55 procedure, not a freely chosen attack.
glossary.Gunflash: Night firing marker or specified equivalent that affects visibility and related night procedures.
glossary.CPVA: Chinese People’s Volunteer Army, with Chapter W nationality and movement rules.
glossary.IPM: Independent Platoon Movement, the CPVA movement procedure in W7.4.
glossary.SAN: Sniper Activation Number, tested only for qualifying Original rolls.
glossary.HOB: Heat of Battle, a triggered resolution rather than an optional action.
glossary.SSR: Scenario Special Rule. It can add or modify applicability and must be included in the scenario profile.
glossary.Source gap: An identified rule reference whose full text is outside the supplied volume. Its details remain unevaluated.
